Question_text: Fig. 2.1 shows a student sitting on a chair. Fig. 2.2 shows the same student with his chair tilted backwards slightly.

Question_text: Fig. 3.1 shows a metal coffee cup on a metal warming plate. There is a small electrical heater inside the warming plate that keeps the plate hotter than the coffee.

This cup is placed on the same type of metal warming plate, but there is a gap filled with air between the base of the cup and the plate.

Parts.part_text: Describe how heat is transferred through the metal and then to all of the liquid in the cup.

A cup of a different shape is placed on the same heater, as shown in Fig. 3.2. The two cups are made of the same metal and contain the same amount of coffee. Explain why the coffee in the cup in Fig. 3.2 is not kept as warm as the coffee in the cup in Fig. 3.1.

Underline which colour and which type of surface is best to keep the coffee warm. black white dull shiny

Question_text: Fig. 5.1 shows an arrangement of three resistors.
image: Two circuit diagrams. Fig. 5.1 shows two 20 Ω resistors connected in parallel, and this parallel combination is then connected in series with a 40 Ω resistor. Question_text: Fig. 6.1 shows a 240V a.c. mains supply connected to a television and two lamps.
image: A circuit diagram illustrating a 240V a.c. mains supply connected to a parallel arrangement of a television (120 W) and two lamps (40 W each). Parts.part_text: In normal operation, the power supplied to each lamp is 40 W and the power supplied to the television is 120 W. Calculate, in normal operation,
the total power supplied,
the total number of kilowatt-hours (kWh) of energy supplied to the circuit in 3.0 hours,
the current in each lamp.

Explain why there is a reading on the voltmeter.

Question_text: A student connects a thermistor in series with a battery and an ammeter. He uses the resistance of the thermistor to determine temperature.

Parts.part_text: In the space below, draw a circuit diagram showing the thermistor, the battery and the ammeter.
The student places the thermistor in a water bath at various temperatures and records the reading on the ammeter. Fig. 11.1 shows how the current varies with temperature.

Specific points shown are approximately 0.10 A at 20°C, 0.20 A at 40°C, and 0.30 A at 60°C.

the resistance of the thermistor at a temperature of 40 °C.
